segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ אִילָן שֶׁהוּא נוֹטֶה לִשְׂדֵה חֲבֵירוֹ – קוֹצֵץ מְלֹא הַמַּרְדֵּעַ, עַל גַּבֵּי הַמַּחֲרֵישָׁה. וּבֶחָרוּב וּבַשִּׁקְמָה – כְּנֶגֶד הַמִּשְׁקוֹלֶת. בֵּית הַשְּׁלָחִין – כׇּל הָאִילָן כְּנֶגֶד הַמִּשְׁקוֹלֶת. אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: כׇּל אִילַן סְרָק כְּנֶגֶד הַמִּשְׁקוֹלֶת.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» With regard to «a tree that leans into the field of another,» the neighbor «may cut» the branches «to the height of an ox goad» raised «over the plow,» in places where the land is to be plowed, so that the branches do not impede the use of the plow. «And» in the case «of a carob tree and» the case «of a sycamore tree,» whose abundance of branches cast shade that is harmful to plants, all the branches overhanging one’s property may be removed «along the plumb line,» i.e., along a line perpendicular to the boundary separating the fields. And if the neighbor’s field is «an irrigated field, all» branches of «the tree» are removed «along the plumb line. Abba Shaul says: All barren trees» are cut «along the plumb line.»
